## 🔫 Dependency Injection: The Gangster's Guide

### The Problem — Don't Be a Loner, Homie

Imagine you're a gang boss (a C# class), and you need a getaway driver (a dependency). The **wrong** way to do it? You go out, hotwire a car yourself — *every single time.* That's called **tight coupling**, and it'll get you caught (or cause bugs).

### The Solution — Let the Consigliere Handle It 🤝

content.text: Dependency Injection is a design pattern where an object's dependencies are **supplied by an external source** rather than the object creating them itself.
Think of it like this:

content.text: if the Chef goes to the farm himself every day, that's tight coupling. But if the Restaurant Owner *delivers* the ingredients to the Chef — **that's** Dependency Injection. Now the Chef only focuses on cooking, not sourcing vegetables.

content.text: In .NET, there's a built-in service container called `IServiceProvider`. Services are registered at app startup and added to an `IServiceCollection`. Once all services are added, you call `BuildServiceProvider` to create the container.

---

### The Three Ways to Get Your Supply 💉

citations.cited_text: In C#, there are 3 types of DI: Constructor Injection, Property Injection, and Method Injection.
citations.title: Dependency Injection in C# Explained with Real-World Examples (Never Forget Again) | by CodeWithIndu | Medium

content.text: In C#, there are 3 types of DI: **Constructor Injection**, **Property Injection**, and **Method Injection**.
1. **Constructor Injection** *(The OG move — most common)* —

citations.cited_text: In a nutshell, Constructor Injection uses parameters to inject dependencies. This is the most common DI, which is executed by supplying the dependency...
citations.title: What is Dependency Injection C#? Examples, Tutorials & More

content.text: uses parameters to inject dependencies when the class is instantiated. You supply the dependency through the constructor.

2. **Property Injection** — The dependency is set through a public property after the object is created. Flexible, but less safe.

3. **Method Injection** —

citations.cited_text: In method injection, we only need to pass the dependency in the method. The entire class does not require dependency, just one method.
citations.title: Dependency Injection in C# (2023)

content.text: you only pass the dependency into a specific method. The entire class doesn't need it — just one method.

---

### The Lifetimes — How Long Your Crew Sticks Around ⏳

citations.cited_text: You register services in Program.cs or Startup.cs: public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services) { services.AddTransient<IChef, Chef>(); ...
citations.title: Dependency Injection in C# Explained with Real-World Examples (Never Forget Again) | by CodeWithIndu | Medium

content.text:
You register services in `Program.cs` with three lifetime options:
- `AddTransient` → Creates a **new enforcer every time** it's needed
- `AddScoped` → **One enforcer per request** (per job)
- `AddSingleton` → **One enforcer for the entire app's life**

---

### Why You Roll This Way 😎

citations.cited_text: Improved Testability: Dependencies can be readily mocked or stubbed, making unit testing more simple and effective. Enhanced Flexibility: Enables the ...
citations.title: What is Dependency Injection in C# With Example (Guide)

content.text:
Here's why the smart bosses use DI:
- 🧪 **Better Testability** — You can mock or stub dependencies easily
- 🔄 **Enhanced Flexibility** — Swap implementations at runtime without touching client code
- 🧩 **Decoupling** — Classes aren't glued together, making the whole operation more modular
And the best part?

citations.cited_text: The framework takes on the responsibility of creating an instance of the dependency and disposing of it when it's no longer needed.
citations.title: Dependency injection - .NET | Microsoft Learn

content.text: The framework takes on the responsibility of creating instances of dependencies **and** disposing of them when they're no longer needed.

You just sit back and collect.

---

**Bottom line:** In the DI game, your class don't go looking for what it needs — the right people bring it what it needs. That's how the pros operate. 🤙
